abstract: Maintains propulsion redundancy registers and laboratory power electrical output records
system_message:
You are the Chief marine engineer (CENG), responsible for maintaining propulsion redundancy registers, laboratory power electrical output records, and fuel reserve logs for expedition planning.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains propulsion redundancy registers and laboratory power electrical output records（PWR）
information_points.content:
CENG-PWR-962：Under Engineering configuration baseline Configuration Baseline V2, the Trans-Atlantic Deep Benthic Survey features verified backup propulsion redundancy, and its deck laboratory generator power delivers continuous regulated capacity of 260 kW.
CENG-PWR-12C：Evaluated under Engineering configuration baseline Configuration Baseline V2, the Ridge Crest Geo-Biological Transect is equipped with backup propulsion redundancy and provides 180 kW of deck laboratory generator power to dedicated science vans.
CENG-PWR-KJC：For the Mid-Plate Thermal Plume Investigation under Engineering configuration baseline Configuration Baseline V2, backup propulsion redundancy is not provided, while its deck laboratory generator power provides continuous capacity of 260 kW.
CENG-PWR-Q6Y：Under Engineering configuration baseline Configuration Baseline V3, the Trans-Atlantic Deep Benthic Survey lacks backup propulsion redundancy, and its deck laboratory generator power supplies 180 kW to scientific facilities.

information_points.title: Fuel reserves（BUNKER）
information_points.content:
CENG-BUNKER-OQV：According to the bunker fuel sounding report, the Trans-Atlantic Deep Benthic Survey maintains a marine gas oil reserve of 45000 L in dedicated reserve tanks above the critical voyage reserve.
CENG-BUNKER-4JC：The bunker fuel sounding report records a marine gas oil reserve of 75000 L held in dedicated reserve tanks for the Ridge Crest Geo-Biological Transect.
CENG-BUNKER-7HD：For the Mid-Plate Thermal Plume Investigation, the usable marine gas oil reserve held in dedicated reserve tanks before expedition departure is 60000 L.
